sections.title: General
sections.description: Launcher-wide options. These are the same in every settings profile.

fields.label: Run at login
fields.help: Adds ~/.config/autostart/luminescent.desktop, which UWSM and most sessions start by themselves. If you also start it from your Hyprland config (exec-once / hl.exec_cmd), remove that so it does not launch twice.

fields.label: Quit everything hotkey
fields.help: Asks for confirmation, then closes Luminescent and every module. The ✕ on the overlay only hides it.

fields.label: Open settings hotkey
fields.help: Opens the overlay straight on the Settings page.

fields.label: Show notifications
fields.help: Small notifications when modules are toggled, things are copied or errors happen.

fields.label: Notification style
fields.help: Reminders and dose warnings always use desktop notifications as well, so they also show up in your notification history.
choices: Luminescent cards (top-right, in the theme's colours)

fields.label: Notifications appear
fields.help: Luminescent cards only. Their colours (and gradients) are in Themes → right-click a theme → Settings… → Notifications.

fields.label: Notification accent
choices: A soft glow of the accent
A stripe down the left side

fields.label: Notifications stay up
fields.help: Long messages always stay up a little longer, and hovering a card keeps it up.

fields.label: Most notifications on screen at once
Notification background
fields.help: Lower lets what is behind show through.

fields.label: Show on start
fields.help: Panels that open by themselves when Luminescent starts.

fields.label: Tray menu
fields.help: What the tray icon's right-click menu lists.

fields.label: List Luminescent in app launchers and docks
fields.help: Adds ~/.local/share/applications/luminescent.desktop and its icon, so Noctalia's launcher and dock show it with the sparkle icon.

fields.label: Tell me when a new version is out
fields.help: Asks GitHub once a day. Tray → Update now downloads it, installs it and restarts; your notes and settings are kept.

fields.label: Show what is new after an update
Keep awake on / off hotkey
fields.help: Stops the screen going dark and the PC going to sleep until you turn it off again (also in the tray, the command palette and the Automation "Keep awake" node).

fields.label: Back up automatically once a week
fields.help: Zips your setup into data/backups (weekly-….zip) and keeps the last 5.

fields.label: Hotkeys also reach the app you are in
fields.help: On (as on Windows): Hyprland runs the hotkey and still passes the keys on. Off: Luminescent's hotkeys are taken away from other apps (Ctrl+B is no longer bold in your editor...).

fields.label: Write a log file (data/launcher.log)
fields.help: Useful for finding out why something went wrong.

sections.title: Overlay & Interface
sections.description: The Luminescent overlay: a dimmed full-screen hub with the Dashboard, Themes, Clipboard and Settings.

fields.label: Open Luminescent
fields.help: Shows the overlay on the Dashboard. Press it again, Esc or ✕ to hide it (it keeps running).

fields.label: Command palette
fields.help: A search box for every action, dashboard item, note, theme and settings page.

fields.label: Hotkey cheat sheet
fields.help: Shows every hotkey while held.

fields.label: Cheat sheet: press to show / press again to hide (instead of hold)
Navigation bar
fields.help: Tick the pages you want in the bar and put them in order. Ctrl+1…9 switch pages while the overlay is open. Notes, Timers and Calculator pages are the same notes, timers and history as the panels.

fields.label: Text size
fields.help: Makes the text in every panel, page, menu and pop-up bigger or smaller.

fields.label: Open on the page I was on last
fields.help: Off: the overlay always opens on the Dashboard.

fields.label: Open the overlay on
fields.help: The page switcher, panels and the dashboard's toolbar go to that screen. Dashboard boxes you put on a particular screen stay there.

fields.label: Panels like Notes open
fields.help: On the screen the overlay opens on. Sticky notes always stay where you put them.
choices: In the middle of the screen

fields.label: Type anywhere on the overlay to search
fields.help: Start typing on the Dashboard or Themes page and the command palette opens with what you typed.

fields.label: Clock and date in the top-left corner
Status strip (running timers, Hearing Guard, next reminder)
Frosted (blurred) background
fields.help: Hyprland blurs what is behind the overlay. Off in performance mode.

fields.label: Glass panels and notifications (blur what is behind them)
fields.help: Hyprland blurs what is behind Notes, the other panels and notifications, so they look like frosted glass. Which windows get it and how see-through they are: theme editor → Glass, where a theme can also have its own.

fields.label: Next theme hotkey
fields.help: Switches to the next theme in the active theme's folder (or the next of all themes).

fields.label: Previous theme hotkey
fields.help: Switches back to the theme before it, the same way round. A theme can also have a key of its own (theme editor → General).

fields.label: Dim the screen behind the overlay
Clicking the dimmed area closes the overlay
fields.help: Around the Themes, Clipboard and Settings panels. The Dashboard works like a desktop: clicking it never closes the overlay, and dragging on it draws a selection box.

fields.label: Apps opened while the overlay is up appear on top of it
fields.help: Super+E, a dashboard item...: the new window floats, centred, above the overlay, and goes back into your tiling layout when the overlay closes.

fields.label: Performance mode
fields.help: No glow, shadows, animations or background images. Use it on a slow PC or while gaming.

fields.label: Show running timers in the tray tooltip
fields.help: Hover the tray icon to see what is left. Only updates while a timer runs.

fields.label: linux-wallpaperengine program
fields.help: Only needed if themes use Wallpaper Engine projects and linux-wallpaperengine is not on PATH.

fields.label: Wallpaper command (optional)
fields.help: Your own command for changing the wallpaper, used by themes and the Automation "Set wallpaper" node instead of the built-in ones. {file} is the picture or video, e.g. mytool set {file}. Blank: Noctalia, swww (plays .gif), hyprpaper or swaybg; videos with mpvpaper.

fields.label: Use the Luminescent colours in the terminal
fields.help: kitty, alacritty and foot windows opened by Luminescent get the theme's colours (passed on the command line, so your terminal config is not touched).

fields.label: Your own terminal follows the theme too
fields.help: Asks first. Linux: adds one include line to ~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf (a backup goes to data/terminal-backups) and writes luminescent-theme.conf next to it, rewritten and reloaded whenever the theme changes. Windows: your PowerShell and Command Prompt profiles in Windows Terminal get the Luminescent colours. Turning it off undoes it.

sections.title: Animations
sections.description: Every animation in Luminescent. Performance mode (Overlay & Interface) turns all of them off.

fields.label: Animations
fields.help: Off: everything appears and moves instantly.

fields.label: Style
fields.help: How things move: Caelestia glides with a little overshoot and panels rise into place.

fields.label: Hover effects
fields.help: Dashboard boxes and cards light up their edge in the accent colour under the mouse.

fields.label: Overlay fades in and out
fields.help: The dimmed hub and everything on it.

fields.label: Switching pages
fields.help: Pages and Settings sections fade in when you switch to them.

fields.label: Sliding marker under the page switcher
Dashboard boxes glide
fields.help: Tidy up, folding, new boxes and boxes moved to another screen.

fields.label: Crossfade when the theme changes
fields.help: The old look fades into the new one instead of jumping.

fields.label: Notifications fade in and out
fields.help: Luminescent's own notification cards.

fields.label: Panels fade in and out
fields.help: Notes, Calculator, Timers and the other floating panels, and the command palette.

fields.label: Smooth zoom on the Automation page
Pulses travelling along Automation wires
fields.help: Only drawn while the Automation page is open.

sections.title: Dashboard & Scripts
sections.description: How dashboard items start.

fields.label: Run scripts (.py, .sh...) in a terminal window
fields.help: Off: they run in the background and their output is not shown.

fields.label: Terminal program
fields.help: e.g. kitty, alacritty, foot. Blank: $TERMINAL, else the first one installed.

fields.label: Keep the script's window open after it finishes
fields.help: So you can read its output and errors.

fields.label: Python for scripts
fields.help: Leave blank to use the Python Luminescent runs with (or the one on PATH for a built version).

fields.label: List dashboard items in the tray menu
Show program and file icons on items
fields.help: Taken from the program's app entry, your icon theme or the file type.

fields.label: Pause between the items of a group (ms)
Tidy up arranges the boxes in
fields.help: Also under the arrow next to Tidy up. With boxes selected only those are tidied; Ctrl+Z puts them back.
choices: Rows (left to right, then the next row)

fields.label: Tidy up order
choices: Keep the order they are in

fields.label: Snap boxes to a grid while moving (px)
fields.help: 0 = off: boxes follow the mouse pixel by pixel, perfectly smooth. Also in the dashboard's right-click menu.

sections.title: Automation
sections.description: The Automation page: nodes you wire together (a timer fires, a command runs, a message pops up…). They run in the background whether or not the overlay is open.

fields.label: Run automations
fields.help: Off pauses every workspace (the Automation page still opens, so you can keep editing).

fields.label: Safety stop: pause a workspace that fires more than this many times a second
fields.help: Stops a wire loop (a node wired back into itself) from freezing Luminescent.

fields.label: Stop a background command after (seconds, 0 = never)

sections.title: Clipboard (Snippets)
sections.description: A folder of files, text and images you can paste with one click. Press the hotkey (or open the Clipboard page), click a card to paste it. Ctrl+click pastes and presses Enter.

fields.label: Snippets folder
fields.help: Sub-folders become folder cards. .txt/.md/.py files paste as text; other files are pasted as files.

fields.label: Paste automatically after clicking
fields.help: When off, the item is only copied to the clipboard.

fields.label: Fill in {date}, {time} and {clipboard} in text snippets
fields.help: When a text snippet is used, {date} becomes today (2026-11-15), {time} the time (14:05), {datetime} both, {weekday} the day and {clipboard} what was on the clipboard before.

fields.label: Columns in the pop-up
fields.help: The Clipboard page in the overlay always shows five.

sections.title: Notes
sections.description: A floating always-on-top notes / to-do panel.

fields.label: Edit mode hotkey
fields.help: Drag the panel by its header any time. Edit mode lets you resize, anchor, add, rename and delete notes.

fields.label: Open straight to the pinned note
fields.help: Showing the panel opens your first pinned note (right-click a note → Pin).

fields.label: Dim the screen in edit mode
Markdown formatting (**bold**, # headings, - lists)
fields.help: Notes are stored as plain text; the 👁 button in a note's header shows it formatted.

sections.title: Screen Doodle
sections.description: Draw on top of everything on screen.

fields.label: Draw hotkey
fields.help: Hold mode: draw while this is held. Toggle mode: press to start/stop drawing. A bare modifier like alt works well with the two options below.

fields.label: Only draw when the key is held on its own
fields.help: Alt+N, Alt+T, Ctrl+Alt+... no longer flash the drawing overlay on: drawing starts after the key has been held alone for the delay below, and Luminescent's own Alt hotkeys cancel it.

fields.label: Hold delay before drawing starts (ms)
fields.help: 0 = instant. 100-150 ms is barely noticeable when you hold the key to draw.

fields.label: Clear drawing when the key is released (hold mode)
Panic hotkey (clear + stop drawing)
fields.help: Esc also stops drawing at any time.

fields.label: Copy screen + drawing hotkey
fields.help: Copies a screenshot of every screen with your drawing on top to the clipboard.

fields.label: Show the tool strip while drawing
fields.help: Pen, highlighter, line, rectangle, circle, arrow, text and the fill toggle. Hold Shift while dragging the pen for a straight line.

fields.label: Start drawing with
fields.help: The tool picked every time you hold (or toggle) the draw key.

fields.label: Mouse wheel changes the brush size while drawing
Tint while drawing
fields.help: A very faint tint so you can tell drawing mode is on.

sections.title: Timer / Stopwatch
sections.description: Floating timers and stopwatches.

fields.label: Edit mode hotkey
fields.help: Edit mode shows reset / switch-mode buttons and the anchor bar.

fields.label: Lap hotkey
fields.help: Records a lap on the stopwatch you started most recently.

fields.label: Flash the panel when a timer finishes
Countdown progress
choices: A thin bar along the bottom

sections.title: Calculator
sections.description: A floating calculator with history. Pin a result and give it a name, then use that name in other sums (e.g. pin 950*12 as rent, then type rent/4).

fields.label: Show / hide hotkey
fields.help: Tip: Enter calculates, Ctrl+Enter calculates, copies and closes, ↑/↓ walk through history. Try 5 km to mi, 20 usd to eur, today + 45 days or 0xff.

fields.label: Fetch currency rates once a day
fields.help: For sums like 20 usd to eur. Rates come from the European Central Bank (frankfurter.app); nothing else is sent.

sections.title: Colour Picker
sections.description: Freeze the screen, zoom in with a loupe and click a pixel to copy its colour. Arrow keys nudge the cursor 1 px, Esc or right-click cancels.

sections.title: Screen Text Grab
sections.description: Drag a box around any text on screen and it is copied to the clipboard. Uses Tesseract: sudo pacman -S tesseract tesseract-data-eng (add tesseract-data-<lang> for other languages).

fields.label: Show the text in an editable box before copying
fields.help: Fix OCR mistakes first, then Copy (Ctrl+Enter).

sections.title: Prompt Log
sections.description: Browse, search and delete your fish, bash or zsh command history, plus everything the Dashboard launched.

sections.title: Keybinds
sections.description: Every keybind on the system in one list: your Hyprland binds (with what they really run) and Luminescent's hotkeys, clashes in red. Add, re-key or remove Hyprland binds; your config file gets the change (a backup goes to data/hypr-backups) and Hyprland reloads it.

sections.title: Ghost Vault
sections.description: Encrypted file storage with a real password, a decoy password and a recovery key.

fields.label: Vault folder (encrypted blobs live here)
fields.help: Must be writable by your user (no sudo). Not under ~/.cache: cleaners empty that.

fields.label: Show picture thumbnails
fields.help: Pictures are decrypted in memory only to draw their thumbnail; nothing is written to disk.

sections.title: Metadata Stripper
sections.description: View and remove metadata from images and videos.

fields.label: Right-click → Strip metadata in Dolphin
fields.help: Adds a Dolphin service menu (~/.local/share/kio/servicemenus). Clean copies go to the folder above and a notification says how many.

sections.title: Hearing Guard
sections.description: Estimates how loud your audio is at the ear (A-weighted, like a sound-level meter), keeps it under a dB limit, and tracks your daily safe listening allowance (NIOSH: 85 dB(A) for 8 h; every +3 dB halves the time).

fields.label: Mode
choices: Limit: dip the volume while over the limit
Record only: keep the readings, never warn or change the volume

fields.label: Limit (estimated dB)
fields.help: 85 dB(A) is the NIOSH recommended maximum for 8 hours a day.

fields.label: Dip the apps, then bring them back when the loud part is over
fields.help: On: the apps playing (not the master volume, so no volume pop-up) are turned down only while something is over the limit, and come back a second or two later, never above the volume you set. Off: Hearing Guard never turns anything up: it lowers the master volume and leaves it there until you turn it up yourself.

fields.label: Never let master volume go above (%)
fields.help: A hard cap that needs no calibration. Over 100 % only matters if your system lets the volume go past 100 % (PipeWire can).

fields.label: Default calibration: dB at 100 % volume with a full-scale tone
fields.help: Used for output devices you have not calibrated. Calibrate… in the panel measures against a phone sound-meter app and stores a value for each device; 100-115 is typical for headphones.

fields.label: Notify at 50 %, 80 % and 100 % of the daily allowance
How your headset's own volume works
fields.help: Only used when you type the volume your headphones show into the panel (Headset's own volume). If halving it there makes the estimate drop far more than you hear, pick the other one.
choices: Like the PC's volume (most headsets and their apps)

fields.label: Captured audio already includes the master volume
fields.help: Leave off. PipeWire records the output's monitor before the master volume, so the volume is added on top. Turn on only if lowering the volume by 6 dB makes the estimate drop by about 12 dB (PipeWire set up with monitor.channel-volumes = true).

sections.title: Reminders
sections.description: Pop-ups, sounds, notifications and theme switches at a set time: once, daily, weekly or every N minutes.

fields.label: Auto-close pop-ups after (seconds, 0 = stay until dismissed)
Fire missed reminders if less than (minutes) late
fields.help: If the PC was asleep or off when a reminder was due, it still fires on wake unless it is later than this.

sections.title: Window Snapper
sections.description: Hotkeys that put the active window in a half, a third or a corner of its screen. The window floats while it is snapped; press a direction again for the next size (half, third, two thirds).

fields.label: Undo (back into tiling on Linux, back where it was on Windows)

sections.title: Screen Ruler
sections.description: Freeze the screen and drag between two points to measure them in pixels. Shift keeps the line level, click copies W×H, Ctrl+click the distance.

sections.title: Media Controls
sections.description: What is playing in any player (Spotify, Firefox, mpv…) with previous / play-pause / next. Needs playerctl: sudo pacman -S playerctl.

sections.title: QR Code
sections.description: Shows the text or link on the clipboard as a QR code to scan with a phone. Copy it as a picture or save it as PNG or SVG.

sections.title: System Monitor
sections.description: CPU, memory, GPU and network with a minute of history in a small floating panel. Only measures while it is on screen.

sections.title: System Settings
sections.description: The computer's own settings: where your monitors are (drag them), resolution, refresh rate, scale and rotation, brightness and night light, the mouse, touchpad and keyboard, Hyprland's gaps, borders and blur, dark mode, power, sound devices and what the computer is.

fields.label: Keep my changes
fields.help: Hyprland forgets changes made while it runs when its config reloads. With this on, Luminescent puts back what you changed in System Settings after a reload and when it starts.

sections.title: Performance
sections.description: Widgets for the CPU, GPU, VRAM, memory, disks, network and temperatures; every app with its CPU, memory, GPU and VRAM; speed settings, Game mode, alerts, startup apps and a gaming HUD. Only measures while it is on screen (or while alerts, rules or automatic Game mode need it).

sections.title: Atlas Sync
sections.description: Swaps notes and timer time with the Atlas app on your phone over Wi-Fi. Press Let Atlas connect, then type the address and code into Atlas → Sync. Atlas shows every change before anything is written.

fields.label: Send my theme to Atlas
fields.help: Your current Luminescent theme shows up in Atlas as "Luminescent: …". Turn on Settings → Themes → Follow Luminescent in Atlas and it switches to it after every sync.

fields.label: Bring Atlas's own themes here
fields.help: Themes you made in Atlas become Luminescent themes named "Atlas: …".

fields.label: Notifications for Atlas events and tasks
fields.help: Atlas's calendar events and tasks come over with every sync; this PC then reminds you of them like your phone does. They are also on the Calendar page.

fields.label: Remind me this many minutes before an event
fields.help: Used when the event has no reminder time of its own in Atlas.

fields.label: Remind me of tasks due today at (hour)

sections.title: Caelestia & Glass
sections.description: The Caelestia shell's config files as forms you can edit (with a backup on every save), its colours and wallpaper, and see-through glass windows per app (focused and unfocused) with the blur strength.

fields.label: Lock the screen hotkey (Caelestia's lock screen)
Caelestia extras: pictures in place of the lyrics and behind the lock screen
Put my colours back when Caelestia rewrites its scheme
fields.help: Colours you saved for a Caelestia scheme (Caelestia & Glass → Colours) come back whenever Caelestia switches to that scheme again or makes it anew (for example from a new wallpaper).

fields.label: Re-theme Caelestia's apps when Luminescent changes its colours
fields.help: After a theme gives Caelestia its colours, Caelestia also re-colours the apps it themes (terminals, btop, GTK and Qt apps, Discord, Spotify...), the same as when it switches scheme itself. Off: only the shell changes.
